symbols.x: an input: the feature values of one example (x_1, x_2 are single features)
symbols.m: the number of training examples; in the tutorial, the boosting round number
symbols.i: counts training examples; in the weighted vote, counts the models
symbols.epsilon: a model's weighted error: the share of the total weight sitting on its mistakes
symbols.alpha: a model's weight in the final vote (tutorial); gradient boosting's step size
symbols.w: an example's weight: how much it counts when training the next model
symbols.y: the true label (+1 or -1 in AdaBoost) or target value of an example
symbols.k: the number of models in the ensemble
symbols.j: counts the models (boosting rounds) in the slides' notation
symbols.lambda: a model's weight: how much say it gets in the final vote
symbols.h: a weak learner: a simple classifier answering +1 or -1 (the tutorial's base model)
symbols.e: Euler's number, about 2.718, raised to a power; as a subscript (W_e), marks the mistakes
symbols.sum: add up the term that follows, once for every value of the index shown
symbols.C: the combined classifier (ensemble) built so far, after a given round
symbols.t: counts the models (boosting rounds or bootstrap samples) built one after another
symbols.L: a base model L_j (slides); in the tutorial, the total exponential loss
symbols.hat:y: the current prediction for an example (in a vote, one model's output)
symbols.J: the loss, which measures training error; J_i is the loss on example i
symbols.W: the total weight of all examples in this round
symbols.sigma: the spread of the noise in the data (sigma squared is the noise variance); in the bagging variance formula, one model's spread
symbols.M: a base model M_t in bagging; in the tutorial product, the total number of rounds
symbols.p: the chance that one model gets the answer wrong
symbols.Z: the total weight after an update, used to rescale the weights to add up to 1
symbols.D: the training dataset; D_t is the bootstrap sample used for model t
symbols.rho: the correlation between two models' predictions: how alike their errors are
symbols.n: the number of training examples (the tutorial's letter; the slides use m)
symbols.c: a subscript meaning correct: W_c is the total weight on correctly classified points
symbols.T: the number of models (trees) to build
symbols.f: the small model fitted to the residuals in gradient boosting
symbols.abs: the size of the set: how many examples it holds
symbols.exp: e raised to the power in brackets
symbols.w:err: a label meaning mistakes: W_err is the total weight on misclassified points
symbols.d: the number of features each random-forest tree gets
symbols.theta: the parameters of a model, which training adjusts
symbols.Y: the class label, treated as a random outcome
symbols.mid: given that: the condition after the bar is known to hold
symbols.w:sign: +1 if the total is positive, -1 if negative
symbols.partial: a partial derivative: how much the quantity changes when only the next variable changes
symbols.cal:R: a region of the feature space that gets one class
symbols.nabla: the gradient: direction in which the loss rises fastest (the slide writes the residual here, which is really the negative)
symbols.prod: multiply the term that follows, once for every value of the index shown
symbols.K: the number of models (the notebook's letter for k)
symbols.bb:E: the expected value: the average over many possible training sets
symbols.hat:f: the model's fitted prediction function, learned from one training set
symbols.w:bias: the error from the model class being unable to capture the true relationship
symbols.w:var: how much the prediction changes from one training set to another
symbols.F: the true target function that generates the data
symbols.infty: infinity: the number of examples keeps growing without limit
symbols.S: one training set drawn from the data distribution
symbols.cal:D: the distribution that training sets are drawn from
symbols.cal:A: the learning algorithm that is run on each bootstrap sample
symbols.P: the probability of the event shown
symbols.w:wrong: marks the case where the models give the wrong answer
symbols.log: the natural logarithm (the notes say natural log)
symbols.w:new: marks the updated weight, after this round
symbols.in: is a member of the set that follows
symbols.cal:X: the set of all possible inputs
symbols.cal:H: the set of candidate weak classifiers to choose from
symbols.w:if correct: the case where the classifier got this point right
symbols.w:if wrong: the case where the classifier got this point wrong

Combining models.alpha: a mixture-of-experts weight that depends on the input, showing a model's expertise there
Combining models.lambda: a model's fixed weight in the vote
Combining models.k: the number of models being combined

Stability.L: the learning algorithm that is trained on each training set
Stability.k: the number of neighbours used in kNN

Bias and variance as a tool.y: the observed target value of an example: true function plus noise
Bias and variance as a tool.sigma: the spread of the noise in the data; sigma squared is noise no model can remove
Bias and variance as a tool.m: the number of training examples, growing without limit

Bagging.sigma: the spread of one model's predictions; sigma squared is one model's variance
Bagging.m: the number of training examples (m' is the bootstrap sample size)

Random forests.k: the number of trees in the forest

Randomization.N: the number of random options a greedy algorithm tries

Gradient boosting.alpha: the step size: how much of each correction is added
Gradient boosting.J: half the sum of squared misses between targets and predictions
Gradient boosting.y: the true target value of an example

Tutorial Q1.alpha: how much say the round's weak learner gets in the ensemble
Tutorial Q1.L: the total exponential loss of the ensemble over all examples
Tutorial Q1.d: a tiny change: dL/d(alpha) is the slope of the loss as alpha changes
Tutorial Q1.C: the ensemble built so far, after a given round
Tutorial Q1.e: Euler's number, about 2.718; as a subscript (W_e), marks the mistakes

Tutorial Q2.x: a feature of a point (x_1, x_2 are its two coordinates)
Tutorial Q2.C: the ensemble after a round (C_3); also the name of point C
Tutorial Q2.D: the name of the fourth point
Tutorial Q2.alpha: how much say the round's weak learner gets in the ensemble
